separations_between_bodies.why: angular separation is invariant under any frame rotation, so it compares light-time, aberration and deflection independently of the precession-nutation model
separations_between_bodies.moon_note: about 2 m at lunar distance; cause not identified

absolute_ra_dec.reading: The difference is the same for every body and varies smoothly with the epoch, i.e. a frame rotation: about +0.23 arcsec in RA in 1900, about +0.05 from 1962 to 2026, about -0.16 in 2100. It is the documented difference between Horizons IAU76/80 of-date frame and the IAU 2006/2000B frame used here, not a property of the bodies.

range.range_rate: Our range rate equals the centered difference of the range that Horizons itself returns to better than 1 mm/s (Mercury 17.740075 vs 17.740074 km/s; Mars -13.033240 vs -13.033240; Moon 0.070360 vs 0.070360, at TDB JD 2452779.5). Horizons own deldot differs from the derivative of its own delta by 1.6 m/s (Mercury), 0.7 m/s (Mars) and 6 mm/s (Moon): a definitional difference, so deldot is not a valid reference for the true range rate.

not_established: agreement of absolute RA/Dec with a frame other than the one Horizons states
